result.title: Joint upper-bound coverage and route-choice utility: an empirical evaluation on two urban proxy tasks
result.summary: Whether more accurate traffic forecasts or higher uncertainty coverage improve route decisions is unclear. We evaluate this question with a frozen protocol that separates speed error, joint candidate path upper bound coverage, route selection, and realized loss. Using processed road speed data from Beijing and Chengdu, we construct offline proxy tasks with 150 origin destination pairs, three candidate paths, and 14 test days per city. We compare raw 90th percentile path time bounds with jointly calibrated upper bounds under minimum bound route choice. Joint coverage rises from 83.19% to 92.26% in Beijing M1, from 75.14% to 88.33% in Chengdu M1, and from 74.01% to 90.64% in Chengdu M2. Yet C2 increases lateness by 0.1633, 0.7848, and 0.9200 percentage points, respectively, and mean travel time by 0.588, 3.082, and 4.418 seconds. In a separate Chengdu predictor comparison, a 14.91% reduction in speed mean absolute error accompanies a 1.4571 percentage point reduction in lateness under C0. Joint coverage is therefore not a surrogate for downstream route utility in these frozen tasks the offline results do not establish online or causal benefits.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文用固化的离线代理任务（北京、成都路网速度数据，150 个 OD 对、三条候选路径、各 14 个测试日）检验联合上界覆盖率与路径选择效用之间的关系，比较原始 90 分位路径时间界与联合校准上界在最小上界路径选择下的表现，发现覆盖率提升并未改善下游出行损失。
AI.relevance_reason: 摘要显示覆盖率提升与错时、平均出行时间增加同时出现，这一「不确定性刻画好≠决策效用好」的解耦结论，可能与 LVR 中「获取更多视觉证据或更高覆盖率并不保证答案收益」及 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的收益—成本权衡形成类比，可供核查评价指标是否应直接对齐下游决策而非中间覆盖率。
